job.style: a diary entry or letter by a student

passage: Dear Diary, today our teacher explained how Siddhartha Gautama left his comfortable life as a prince to seek the truth about suffering. He realized that our constant cravings, or 'tanha', for worldly things cause us pain, not just physical thirst. He wanted everyone to understand his message, so he taught in Prakrit, the common language of the people, instead of the complex Sanskrit used by priests. We also learned about Mahavira, who taught that 'ahimsa' means showing kindness to all living creatures, including insects and plants, not just humans. Later, we discussed the Upanishads. It was fascinating to learn that thinkers like Gargi were famous for their deep knowledge and participated in royal debates, proving that women were active scholars. We also learned that the Sangha was a place where monks lived together. These Viharas were not built by kings with tax money, but were often donated by wealthy merchants or landowners who supported the monks' simple lives. Finally, we explored the idea of the Atman, the individual soul, and Brahman, the universal soul, which are philosophical concepts about the nature of existence, not physical gods living in the sky.

items.evidence: He wanted everyone to understand his message, so he taught in Prakrit, the common language of the people, instead of the complex Sanskrit used by priests.
items.q: Why did the Buddha teach in Prakrit rather than Sanskrit?
options: Ordinary people could follow the language easily
Only scholars could follow the language easily
Priests asked him to use a simpler language
Sanskrit had not yet been invented then
items.explain: He wanted everyone to understand his message, so he used the common language of the people.

wrong.why: thinks he taught in a scholars' language
picks the priests named nearby as the cause
guesses a reason using outside ideas

items.evidence: He realized that our constant cravings, or 'tanha', for worldly things cause us pain, not just physical thirst.
items.q: A boy always wants a newer phone and feels unhappy. Which idea of the Buddha explains this?
options: Constant craving for things causes pain
Being thirsty for water causes pain
Owning many things removes all pain
Ruling a large empire ends pain
items.explain: The Buddha taught that constant cravings, or tanha, for worldly things cause us pain.

wrong.why: thinks tanha means thirst for water
reverses cause and effect of cravings
thinks the Buddha was a ruling king

items.evidence: We also learned about Mahavira, who taught that 'ahimsa' means showing kindness to all living creatures, including insects and plants, not just humans.
items.q: A student follows Mahavira's ahimsa. How would they treat an ant on the path?
options: Step around it to avoid harming it
Ignore it because it is not human
Move it away because it is a pest
Feed it only on festival days
items.explain: Ahimsa means kindness to all living creatures, including insects, not just humans.

wrong.why: treats insects as harmful things to remove
thinks kindness is only for special days

items.evidence: These Viharas were not built by kings with tax money, but were often donated by wealthy merchants or landowners who supported the monks' simple lives.
items.q: How were many Viharas, where monks lived, paid for?
options: Rich merchants and landowners gave gifts
Kings spent money collected from taxes
Monks sold crops grown on their land
Villagers paid a fee to every visitor
items.explain: Viharas were often donated by wealthy merchants or landowners who supported the monks' simple lives.

wrong.why: thinks the government paid with taxes
guesses monks funded their own homes
guesses a fee system from outside ideas
